name: UK General Data Protection Regulation and Data Protection Act 2018, as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025
status_note: UK GDPR is the retained version of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 in force since the end of the transition period (31 December 2020). The Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 amended it in stages. Article 12A on response time was inserted from 5 February 2026 (S.I. 2026/82). The duty to handle complaints first at controller level (DPA 2018 s. 164A) applies fully from 19 June 2026. From 30 September 2026 legislation.gov.uk shows the regulator referred to as the Commission (S.I. 2026/386 and S.I. 2026/1015). The ICO website still uses the ICO name.

rights.summary: The data subject can obtain erasure without undue delay where a listed ground applies, including no longer necessary, withdrawn consent, a successful objection under Art. 21, or unlawful processing.

The data subject can object to processing based on legitimate interests, public task or recognised legitimate interests, and the controller must stop unless it shows compelling legitimate grounds, and can object to direct marketing at any time.
A person can ask a search engine to remove results for searches on their name, using the same erasure and objection rights.
The data subject can obtain a copy of their data and information about its source.
The data subject can have inaccurate data corrected.

deadline.extension_note: One month beginning with the relevant time, which is the latest of receipt of the request, receipt of any identity information requested under Art. 12(6), and payment of any permitted fee (Art. 12A(1) and (2)). The controller may extend by two further months for complexity or number of requests by notice with reasons given within the first month (Art. 12A(3) and (4)). For access requests only, the clock pauses while the controller waits for clarification it reasonably needs (Art. 12A(5)). Before complaining to the regulator, the person should complain to the controller, which must acknowledge the complaint within 30 days and respond without undue delay (DPA 2018 s. 164A).

regulators.name: Information Commission (operating as the Information Commissioner's Office, ICO)
regulators.note: Complaints under DPA 2018 s. 165. The ICO asks for a copy of the complaint already made to the organisation and of the original request, and a letter of consent if complaining for someone else. It prioritises cases with serious harm and says detailed cases are assigned around 10 months after submission.

identity_verification: Where the controller has reasonable doubts about identity it may ask for additional information needed to confirm it and may delay dealing with the request until identity is confirmed (UK GDPR Art. 12(6)). The one-month clock then starts when that information is received (Art. 12A(2)(b)).

authorized_agent.note: UK GDPR does not regulate representation directly. The ICO accepts complaints made for another person with a letter of consent from that person. Use a signed authorisation for requests made on someone's behalf.

special_channels.name: Google personal information removal request under European privacy law
special_channels.note: Google's Right to be Forgotten overview links to this form for countries that apply European data protection law. Whether Google applies it to the UK was not stated on the overview page, so check the country list in the form.

special_channels.name: Bing request form to block search results in Europe
special_channels.note: The country list on the form includes the United Kingdom.

public_records_note: UK GDPR has no general exemption for publicly available data, so a people-search site needs a lawful basis, usually legitimate interests, which an Art. 21 objection challenges. Erasure does not apply where processing is necessary for freedom of expression and information, a legal obligation, archiving or research under Art. 84B, or legal claims (Art. 17(3)). DPA 2018 Schedule 2 adds further exemptions, including for journalistic, academic, artistic and literary purposes.
